review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner; self-review, not independent approval
review.decision: Recover a transient post-admission binding failure without guessing the current thread or weakening terminal identity
review.notes: User requests current session association fix. Runtime diagnosis proved inherited TMUX_PANE %10 is another project; actual current gtmux dev is %23. Current valid terminal inspection succeeds; matching bridge log has a prior failed Bind and source has no pending retry. This is proof of lost recovery behavior, not the exact missing observation at17:25. Design precedes tests. Retain only a matching successful root operation already observed on the home-verified, admitted live connection. Do not infer SID from CWD, inherited pane, shared backend, argv, global notifications or history reads. Keep all existing strict PID/birth/home/foreground/TTY/new-owner/epoch checks. Retry only explicitly unavailable observation or held publication lease; observed different identity and unsafe IO remain refused. A state helper is wired into actual Run bind/tick/selection paths; deterministic baseline callback/tick negative control is semantics extracted from exact B, not a whole B binary/real reconnect. Controller retries publication only, never protocol frames, task input, service/terminal restart or restore. Suspend old-root heartbeat after a successful different-root operation while new binding is unresolved. Preserve committed receipt-error handling and all current observer protection tests. Native/UI runtime acceptance of the existing old bridge is separate from candidate source quality; do not fabricate a live rebind. Shared dirty root and frozen PR1859/1861 source remain unchanged.

cases.description: Typed binding readiness preserves strict identity and distinguishes unavailable proof
cases.setup: Actual BindCodexFrontend and isolated process/pane/storage seams
cases.action: Temporarily omit bridge/backend/terminal observations then restore; compare changed birth, home, target and newer owner
cases.expected: Missing observations remain refused but retryable. Explicit observed identity/home/birth/owner mismatch is hard and never publishes. Existing input authority assertions remain unchanged.

cases.description: A verified root operation survives one transient binding failure
cases.setup: Production observer plus production per-connection binding state; deterministic clock and strict bind/refresh seams, no real daemon
cases.action: Receive matching successful root response, fail first binding, tick after proof recovers; include initial empty attachment and same-root reconnect
cases.expected: The exact root is retried within schedule/budget and binds once, then ordinary heartbeat resumes; no repeated root RPC or message/input is sent. Baseline callback/tick semantics fail the recovery assertion.

cases.description: Pending retry cannot publish stale roots or exceed its budget
cases.setup: Same production state/observer, controlled selection/epoch/clock/lease/receipt failures
cases.action: New root request before response, newer accepted root, old response, invalid/ephemeral/home/notification/catalog traffic, new connection epoch, hard mismatch, receipt-only error and deadline
cases.expected: New selection invalidates prior pending root; old responses/epochs never reclaim. Unknown observations do not authorize. Hard mismatch stops. At most8 bind attempts, no new attempt at/after30s, exponential1/2/4/8s pacing. Deadline is scheduling bound, not a claim that an uninterruptible syscall returns at30s. Receipt-only errors retain committed attachment and retry only via ordinary heartbeat. A newer successful root whose binding fails suspends old-root heartbeat instead of keeping wrong history live.
